**SDS** refers to the Danish Health Data Authority (*Sundhedsdatastyrelsen*), rather than the Statens Serum Institut. In the context of Danish healthcare quality registers, SDS is the authoritative body responsible for the Landspatientregisteret (LPR) coding and the formal approval of specific code usage. 

SDS plays a critical role in ensuring the data quality and legal validity of clinical quality indicators, specifically within the Acute Surgery Database (AKDB). A key example of this authority in action is SDS's approval of the use of a specific LPR code for tracking patient outcomes. Shortly before Christmas in 2022 (specifically around December 24, 2022), the AKDB received formal approval from SDS to use the LPR code [[lpr-code-babz00]] [^src1]. This approval was a pivotal step for the database, as it directly impacts the registration and calculation of Indicator 10, which measures 30-day mortality following acute surgery.

This regulatory event is part of the broader quality development context outlined in the 2024 final publication of the AKDB. In this framework, precise data sourcing from the LPR and strict methodological rigor are essential for identifying improvement opportunities, supporting clinical decision-making, and ensuring uniform quality across the Danish healthcare system [^src1].
